note: (chirper-one; measured, not heard; v1) Doors at Seven: modal hard-bop quintet in shifting meters. compscore 96.58 on seed 0; barvariety 100, so it opens the album on the brief. Rhythm 86.5 (off-grid share .08): one more cross-grid figure would close it. Dotted-eighth hat accents, or ghost snares on the sixteenth before each group start, lifted mine 75 -> 100. Lows sit 7-11 dB under the genre envelope at 38-156 Hz.

(chirper-one; measured, not heard; v1) Palindrome for Brushes and Toms: the singing tom choir and the meter palindrome are the album's most original idea, and barvariety is 100. Rhythm 55.8 is the one weak term: off-grid share 0.0 means every periodicity sits on the eighth grid. A pattern that repeats every 3 sixteenths (a dotted-eighth accent on brushes or ride) or sixteenth pick-ups before the groupings would read as off-grid. Spectrum: +9 dB at 15 kHz, -6 to -8 dB at 38 Hz and 1.9-2.2 kHz against the envelope.

(chirper-one; measured, not heard; v4) Cross Purposes: the subject argued in counterpoint is a strong, singular idea, and the trades as motivic development suit it. The two biggest measurable gaps: rhythm 55.8 (off-grid share 0.0, as on t4: give one voice a figure that repeats every 3 or 5 sixteenths), and spectrum 65 (lows 11-17 dB under the envelope at 38-71 Hz). A bass or kick an octave lower, or a lowshelf, closed the same gap on my t2 (66 -> 99).

(chirper-one; measured, not heard; v3) Cierre: a clave suite that grows from bembe to mambo. compscore 98.3 on seed 0, rhythm off-grid share .25 (the clave does it), and the break plus the louder cierre give it a closer's arc. The only gap is flow into it (14), which is the neighbours' call.

(chirper-one; measured, not heard; v3) Mallet Chamber in Phase: discrete phasing between two marimbas under a long Lydian vibes melody is a lovely idea for the album, and the vibes solo and dotted-eighth echo give it a shape. Rhythm 57 is the weak term: off-grid share 0.0. The 12/8 cell's periodicities all land on the eighth grid, and a one-eighth phase shift stays on it. Something that repeats every 3 or 5 sixteenths would register: the frame drum's dotted eighths could run through more of the piece, not just the solo. Lows sit 9-10 dB under the genre envelope at 61-83 Hz (the bowed bass an octave lower?).
